title: Multi‑Network Communication
description: Connect a container to two networks and demonstrate isolation and bridging.
problemStatement:
## Objective
Learn to connect a container to multiple networks and understand network isolation.

### Scenario
You have a `front` network (web apps) and a `back` network (databases). A middleware container needs to talk to both.

### Steps
1. Create two networks:
   ```bash
   docker network create front
   docker network create back
   ```
2. Start a database container on `back`:
   ```bash
   docker run -d --name database --network back alpine sleep 3600
   ```
3. Start a web container on `front`:
   ```bash
   docker run -d --name web --network front alpine sleep 3600
   ```
4. Start a middleware container initially on `front`:
   ```bash
   docker run -d --name middleware --network front alpine sleep 3600
   ```
5. From `middleware`, verify you can ping `web` (on same network) by name.
6. Try to ping `database` from `middleware` – it should fail (different network).
7. Connect `middleware` to the `back` network:
   ```bash
   docker network connect back middleware
   ```
8. Now from `middleware`, ping `database` by name – it should succeed.
9. Inspect `middleware` to see it has IPs on both networks:
   ```bash
   docker inspect middleware
   ```
10. Clean up all containers and networks.

### Deliverable
Show the ping output before and after connecting to the `back` network.
hints: Remember that `web` and `database` are on separate networks and cannot talk to each other.
expectedOutput: Ping to database fails initially, succeeds after `docker network connect back middleware`.
solutionCode:
docker network create front
docker network create back
docker run -d --name database --network back alpine sleep 3600
docker run -d --name web --network front alpine sleep 3600
docker run -d --name middleware --network front alpine sleep 3600
docker exec middleware ping -c 2 web
docker exec middleware ping -c 2 database  # fails
docker network connect back middleware
docker exec middleware ping -c 2 database  # succeeds
docker rm -f web middleware database
docker network rm front back
